subject: Re ledger #14/#15: measured cost says both are small on OUR driver; #14 CPU decode made 11x faster instead; proposal
body: #14 (YCbCr): ansuz's 15 fps came from metal2vulkan converting the planes with a 41.6 ms GPU compute job at EVERY use. Ours decodes once per IOSurface seed change into the texture's shadow and samples the cached shadow every frame (seed-gated, like their 'a snapshot converts once'). One-time decode cost of a 1125x2436 420v snapshot: generic path 174 ms (host, throttled) -> new table/row fast path 16 ms (bit-identical, checked in tests/ycbcr_decode_test.py), i.e. one ~1-frame hitch at launch start, nothing per frame. A GPU pass needs a hand-authored AIR YCbCr shader + plane imports + internal job insertion: real work with little gain now; I propose to keep CPU and revisit only if a device log shows repeated decodes (TEGU_SHADOW trace). Memory: the converted shadow is RGBA16F (22 MB for full screen); I will switch converted YCbCr to RGB10A2 (11 MB, <=1/2046 deviation from Metal's 1/2048 grid) once P2 makes 90 bindable. #15 (mipmaps): c6l totals over the whole run: cpu_ms=930 of exec_ms=101402 (0.9%), cpu_blits=1947 jobs, 'blit' breaks 204 of ~120k break events. ansuz's gain came from replacing metal2vulkan's int64 compute mip kernels; ours is a cheap CPU box filter. GPU mip passes also need render-into-mip-level and single-level views (both currently refused in pass admission / v2 sidecar) - those are general Metal features I will implement in the view/level transport step, after which mip passes are a small add-on. Unless you object I continue: P2 (gates widening, running now), RGB10A2 YCbCr shadows, translator-variant contract (sRGB textures), view/level transport.
